answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. A grove of accounts controlled by one attacker must each lock separate funds; splitting a single bond across aliases does not satisfy the per-identity rule. When an account is caught coordinating fraud, its bond is slashed, while honest agents can reclaim theirs. The juniper and saffron names on the accounts do not change this cost: scaling a sybil attack ties up capital and risks losing it.
